title: Cross-Model In-Context Neurofeedback Reveals (Limited) Activation Control in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.20179v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Probes on activation vectors are widely used to detect misbehavior in language models, but their success relies on the assumption that models cannot control what their activations encode. Humans can learn, through neurofeedback, to control the firing of even single neurons, and recent studies investigated whether this ability extends to language models, reaching conflicting conclusions. No experimental design so far disentangles competence at the task from genuine access to one's own activations. We fill this gap with in-context neurofeedback sessions, in which a "subject" model is asked to maximize (or minimize) a score derived from its activations, shown back to it at every turn. In our first experiment, the sentences are generated either by the subject or by a second "writer" model, while the score always derives from the activations of the subject. We test ten open-weight models from five families, with sizes from 9B to 32B. Some mod

translated_title: 跨模型上下文内神经反馈揭示大语言模型中的（有限）激活控制能力
translated_abstract: 基于激活向量的探针被广泛用于检测语言模型的不良行为，但其有效性依赖于一个假设：模型无法控制其激活所编码的内容。人类可以通过神经反馈学会控制甚至单个神经元的放电，近期有研究探讨了这种能力是否也适用于语言模型，但得出了相互矛盾的结论。迄今为止，尚无实验设计能够将模型在任务上的表现能力与其对自身激活的真实访问区分开来。我们通过“上下文内神经反馈”会话填补了这一空白：在其中，一个“受试”模型被要求最大化（或最小化）一个由其自身激活计算得出的分数，且该分数会在每一轮对话中展示给该模型。在我们的第一个实验中，句子要么由受试模型自己生成，要么由第二个“写作”模型生成，而分数始终来自受试模型的激活。我们测试了来自五个系列的十个开源权重模型，规模从9B到32B。部分模型……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文提出跨模型上下文内神经反馈新范式，首次将模型在任务上的胜任能力与对自身激活的真实访问区分开来，测试十个开源大模型后发现大语言模型仅具备有限的激活控制能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a cross-model in-context neurofeedback paradigm that, for the first time, disentangles task competence from genuine access to a model's own activations, revealing only limited activation control in LLMs across ten open-weight models from five families.
